The knowledge and sight named in 17:17 let the bringing-out be heard as disclosure to the bearer.

findings.containment: This is a bounded image built from the focus sequence, not a claim that an animal is literally tied to the neck or that the book is physically carried there. epistemic.reason: The channel support is trusted and each contact is visible in supplied focus/context wording; the dossier is a bounded synthesis, not a literal gloss of one word.

findings.title: Haste becomes itemized self-reading
findings.claim: The pericope moves from human haste in 17:11 to counting and detailed separation in 17:12; the focus then brings each person an open book, 17:14 commands its bearer to read it, and 17:15 makes the burden nontransferable. Together, these contacts picture the record as a counter-tempo that unfolds impulse into an accountable self-reading.
findings.mechanism: Haste is the contextual problem; reckoning and detailed articulation break action into legible parts. The focus's written kitab and open manshur state supply the record, 17:14 makes the bearer its reader, and 17:15 prevents another person from carrying the account instead. The focus book thus returns the sequence of impulse as an ordered object its own subject must read.
findings.reader_payoff: The record appears as a way that compressed action becomes countable and readable by the person who owns it.
findings.containment: The counter-tempo is an attributed synthesis, not a claim that every deed was deliberate or that the verses state a theory of time. The book remains an account; manshuran means open/spread here and does not establish a ruler's unsealed document. The HFT's alternative, adjacent judgment features without a deliberate counter-tempo, remains live.

epistemic.reason: The exact sequence and trace roles are present in the pericope; the counter-tempo synthesis and its alternative are explicitly attributed.

findings.title: The account carries a chosen course
findings.claim: 17:18-21 distinguishes desired destinations, immediate acceleration, purposeful striving, provision, and graded outcomes. Those contacts return through the focus's flight-bearing tair, its scope over every person, and what each person meets, so the book can be read as preserving a direction and its achieved level rather than only a heap of separate acts.
findings.mechanism: The context supplies desire at 17:18, striving and recognized effort at 17:19, provision for both groups at 17:20, and degrees at 17:21. The focus's flight image carries direction, kull makes the account distributive, and yalqahu makes the person meet its result; the context sequence therefore changes the attached record into a trajectory with an end and a grade.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a personal account as holding not only actions but the direction in which desire was enacted and the result encountered.
findings.containment: The vector is an attributed synthesis, not a claim that the person controls every outcome or that the context reduces judgment to a single destination. The alternative remains that the book inventories discrete deeds and the later passages discuss outcomes alongside it.

epistemic.reason: All source roots and coordinates match the supplied 17:18-21 and focus occurrences; trajectory-level organization remains an attributed inference.

findings.title: A written bond as an attributed echo
findings.claim: Alongside the ordinary personal-account sense, the focus can carry an exploratory legal echo: an imposed obligation at the neck and a written kitab, read beside the servant word in 17:3, resemble a personal bond document.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies the written-object carrier, the binding verb, and its bodily location; 17:3 supplies an occurrence of abd that the HFT attributes to servitude. Their contact makes the specialized manumission-contract branch audible by analogy, changing the record into a possible written bond attached to its bearer.
findings.reader_payoff: The book can also be imagined as terms attached to a person, adding a relational bond image to the account while leaving the account itself in place.
findings.containment: This remains an attributed analogy, not the syntax's denotation: 17:3 calls Noah a servant of God and does not establish human ownership; 17:13 gives no installments, payment, release, or freed person. The ordinary record reading remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The exact 17:3 root/word coordinate and focus return match the packet, but the legal relation is a surprising multi-step HFT analogy with no independent ownership or emancipation evidence.

findings.title: Shared guidance and the individual book
findings.claim: In 17:2 the Book is given as guidance to the Children of Israel; in 17:13 each person encounters an indefinite, personal book. The shared written-text branch makes the focus's record a personal counterpart to the earlier guidance text, with a different recipient and function.
findings.mechanism: The focus kitab is the carrier; the earlier kitab joined to huda for a people is the independent trigger. Their contact shifts the image from a book received for communal direction to a written account each person must meet and read.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the focus's kitab is a personal record rather than simply another use of the community's guidance scripture.
findings.containment: This is a contrast of function within the supplied pericope, not an equation of the two books, their authority, or their contents. The personal record does not become guidance merely because both are written books.

epistemic.reason: The two Arabic occurrences and their roles are supplied; the personal-counterpart relation is an inference from the context connection nomination, which carries no trust label.

findings.title: Personal accountability within a shared plea
findings.claim: The focus assigns each person an account that stays with them, while the Fātiḥa overlay speaks of worship and help-seeking in the plural and asks for guidance. The personal course can therefore remain individually answerable within a collectively voiced request for aid.
findings.mechanism: The focus's imposed binding on each person is the carrier; 1:5's collective request for help and 1:6's request for a straight path are independent triggers. Their contact distinguishes responsibility from self-sufficiency: the course belongs to the person even as guidance is sought together.
findings.reader_payoff: Individual answerability and shared dependence on guidance can be seen at once, without transferring one person's account to another.
findings.containment: This is a macro overlay from the explicitly added 1:5-1:6 members, not a reading supplied by 17:13 alone. It does not make the record collective, erase personal responsibility, or promise that every requested path has the same outcome.

epistemic.reason: The cited external Arabic and focus form are exact, but their cross-surah relation is a bounded inference and no trust label is supplied for the context projection.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi, kendisine dışarıdan yöneltilen bir işlemle belirli bir şeyden sorumlu veya ona uymakla yükümlü hale getirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus Form IV verb imposes a personal attachment on each bearer.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: In 1:5 the plural speakers ask You for help; in 1:6 they ask to be guided to the straight path.
branch_activations.activation: The personal binding meets a shared request for help and guidance, so individual responsibility is not recast as independence from aid.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Each person remains bound to their own course within a collectively voiced seeking of guidance.
branch_activations.boundary: The external members add a shared petition; they do not transfer the focus account or determine its outcome.
